key_insight: DiagTrace evaluates whether LLMs can reconstruct documented diagnostic trajectories by gathering information interactively, rather than receiving all patient details upfront.
clinical_relevance: The benchmark tests incremental evidence gathering relevant to clinical reasoning, without establishing safety or effectiveness in patient care.
method: Build cases from PubMed Central reports with an initial presentation, event bank, clinical course, and diagnostic references.
Evaluate interactive information seeking against source-documented diagnostic trajectories.
Measure clinical-course alignment, interaction quality, and efficiency.
evidence_signal: DiagTrace contains 510 cases across eight specialties; evaluation of four LLMs on 225 cases revealed trade-offs in coverage, source-consistent ordering, and turn use.
watch_item: Alignment with published case-report trajectories may not reflect diagnostic quality or performance in real-world clinical workflows.
paper_title: DiagTrace: An Interactive Benchmark for Clinical Decision Making
